Draw new response values from the conditional distribution of the response

Source: R/gamm4-methods.R, R/posterior-samples.R
predicted_samples.Rd

Predicted values of the response (new response data) are drawn from the fitted model, created via stats::simulate() (e.g. simulate.gam()) and returned in a tidy, long, format. These predicted values do not include the uncertainty in the estimated model; they are simply draws from the conditional distribution of the response.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
predicted_samples(model, ...)

predicted_samples(model, ...)

# Default S3 method
predicted_samples(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
predicted_samples(
  model,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  marginalise = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'scam'
predicted_samples(
  model,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  n_draws = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  weights = NULL
)

Arguments

model

a fitted model of the supported types; see diagnostic_support.

...

arguments passed to other methods. For fitted_samples(), these are passed on to mgcv::predict.gam(). For posterior_samples() these are passed on to fitted_samples(). For predicted_samples() these are passed on to the relevant stats::simulate() method.

data

data frame; new observations at which the posterior draws from the model should be evaluated. If not supplied, the data used to fit the model will be used for data, if available in model.

n_draws

positive integer; number of response replicates to generate at the fitted parameters. Required; coefficient chains are not used.

seed

numeric; a random seed for the simulations.

weights

numeric; response sampling weights for GAM methods. An explicit vector overrides the fitting weights; a single value applies to every observation. With data = NULL, the default is the fitted prior weights, except factor-valued binomial responses retain one Bernoulli trial per observation. Native mgcv::gaulss() ignores fitting weights in its likelihood, so its default response weights are also ones; explicitly supplied sampling weights still override this default. With prediction data, weights default to a vector of ones. For ordinary Gaussian and Gamma responses, larger weights reduce response variance (precision weights). For binomial responses, weights give integer trial counts. They do not alter the fitted coefficient covariance. Include positions restored by stats::na.exclude() when supplying weights for fitting rows.

marginalise

NULL retains the usual predictions. TRUE selects all supported re and fs terms; character vectors select exact smooth labels. Fitted predictions integrate response means over new zero-mean Gaussian effects. Response samplers draw new effects before sampling responses. Smoothing parameters and dispersion remain fixed. Only ordinary mgcv::gam() and mgcv::bam() fits with a scalar response mean are supported.

Value

A tibble (data frame) with 3 columns containing the posterior predicted values in long format. The columns are

  • .row (integer) the row of data that each posterior draw relates to,

  • .draw (integer) an index, in range 1:n_draws, indicating which draw each row relates to,

  • .response (numeric) the predicted response for the indicated row of data.

Details

LSS response simulation uses all fitted distribution parameters at the requested data, with the same parameter transformations and offset rules as posterior_samples(). It holds coefficients fixed, so it has no coefficient chains or attached coefficient diagnostics.

See also

gamm4_support

Author

Gavin L. Simpson

Examples

load_mgcv()
dat <- data_sim("eg1", n = 120, seed = 2)
m <- gam(y ~ s(x0, k = 6) + s(x2, k = 6), data = dat, method = "REML")

# Simulate responses at new predictor values using the fitted model
newd <- data.frame(x0 = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8), x2 = 0.5)
predicted_samples(m, n_draws = 5, data = newd, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 15 x 3
#>     .row .draw .response
#>    <int> <int>     <dbl>
#>  1     1     1     11.7 
#>  2     2     1      7.89
#>  3     3     1      9.49
#>  4     1     2      9.66
#>  5     2     2     10.6 
#>  6     3     2      8.19
#>  7     1     3     12.1 
#>  8     2     3      9.19
#>  9     3     3     14.1 
#> 10     1     4      7.74
#> 11     2     4     13.1 
#> 12     3     4     14.8 
#> 13     1     5      4.08
#> 14     2     5      8.68
#> 15     3     5      8.12
